Name: Plains Minnow - Hybognathus placitus
Habitat: Montana native. Large, quiet rivers, weedy areas.
Foods: Feeds on bottom ooze. Algae, mimute animals.
Economics: Food source for predatory species.
Name: Fathead Minnow - Pimephales promelas
Habitat: Montana native. Hardy fish, can survive in numerous habitats. Lakes, streams, swamp.
Foods: Algae, detritus, insects larvae, zeoplankton
Economic: Good forage fish.
Name: Longnose Dace - Rhinichthys cataractae
Habitat: Montana native. Wide distribution. Swift cold streams to warm muddy lakes and ponds.
Foods: Bottom feeder. Aquatic insect, larvae, fish eggs, algae.
Economics: Important forage fish.
Name: River Carpsucker - Carpoides carpio
Habitat: Montana native. Warmer lakes, streams and rivers, brackish waters.
Foods: Algae, dratoms, desmids, crustaceans, molluscs, rotefers, aquatic insects, larvae.
Name: Shorthead Redhorse - Moxostoma macrolepidotum
Habitat: Montana native. Streams and rivers, swift, shallow water, clean rocky bottoms.
Foods: Aquatic insects, crustaceans, deatoms, worms, molluscs.
Economics: Fair food fish.
Name: Longnose Sucker - Catostomus catostomus
Habitat; Montana native. Prefers clear lakes streams and rivers but found in warmer, more turbid waters.
Foods: Aquatic invertebrates and plants.
Economics: Provide forage for pedatory species. Flesh sometimes eaten by man.
Name: White Sucker - Catostomus commerson
Habitat: Wide-spread in all habitat types except very cold, very fast water.
Foods: Aquatic invertibrates and plants.
Economics: Provide forage for predatory species. Flesh sometimes eaten by man.
Name: Mountain Sucker - Catostomus platyrhynchus
Habitat: Streams and rivers. Seldom in lakes.
Foods: Diatoms, other algae, lighter plants, dysterous larvae.
Economics: May be important as a forage fish.
Name: Black Bullhead - Ictalurus melas
Habitat: Probably introduced species. Shallow ponds, lakes and backwaters of streams. Tolerant of poor quality water.
Foods: Omnivorous. Aquatic insects, fish, crayfish, worms, snails,
